relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR pauses booking and escalates "no calendar availability" when the derived free-slot list is empty
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When the AI SDR's availability lookup returns no candidate slots, the workflow escalates to a human with "the assigned call host has no available time slots within the configured booking window" and pauses the conversation. The list can be empty while the calendar genuinely has room, so the SDR stops answering positively-responding prospects and the operator is sent to inspect a working calendar.

## Problem

The operator sees an AI SDR paused with a "No meeting times available" banner instructing them to review the calendar and availability limits, on a calendar that already holds meetings the AI SDR itself booked. Affected prospects receive no reply at all after a positive response. Documented behaviour for this state is to ask the prospect for their preferred times.

## Root cause

`offer-alternatives.ts` treats a successful `getTimeSlots` call that returns zero rows as proof the calendar is unavailable and escalates with `ESCALATION_REASONS.NO_CALENDAR_AVAILABILITY`. Added by bbf62d99 ("escalate when calendar has no slots", ENG-11895). The availability fetch has its own failure codes (`CALENDAR_DISCONNECTED`, `CALENDAR_SYNC_FAILED`) which slot-matchmaking already escalates on, so an empty successful result is a different condition and is not distinguished from it.

The empty result itself is arithmetic. `BookingService.getTimeSlots` builds the candidate slot at meeting duration plus the host's before/after buffers, and every existing appointment is represented as busy with its own stored `buffer_before_in_minutes` / `buffer_after_in_minutes`. In short work windows a small number of buffered bookings tiles the window completely, so the candidate set empties while the calendar still has room outside the host's configured availability hours.

The escalation also pre-empts the shipped fallback: `reply-directive.ts` `hasNoCalendarAvailability` → `ASK_FOR_PREFERENCES`, and the help centre states that when no slot passes the filters the AI SDR asks the prospect for their times. `workflow.ts` short-circuits on `ctx.state.escalate` before copywriter and send, so no reply is produced.

## Who's affected

Up to 6 Oct 2026, the AI SDR paused 391 conversations in 65 workspaces this way, with 399 escalation messages. The first was on 7 Sep 2026 and the latest on 6 Oct 2026, so it's still happening. When this ticket was written on 18 Sep 2026, the count was 166 messages in 26 workspaces.

The attached list, `ENG-14028-affected-workspaces.md`, gives each workspace's name and slug, its count and dates, the call host whose calendar the AI SDR checked, and the workspace owners.

We don't know how many other workspaces could hit this. We only see the problem when a conversation is paused, because we don't log how many free slots each lookup finds.

We also haven't proved the cause in every workspace. Our reproduction showed that a buffer of 30 minutes or more before each meeting can fill a short working day, so no free slot is left. When the ticket was written, 9 of the 26 workspaces had a buffer like that. Another 5 had 15-minute buffers before and after each meeting and only 4 to 8 hours of availability a week. The other 12 had smaller buffers or really were busy. We haven't rebuilt each workspace's free slots to confirm this.

Counted on the read-only production replica on 6 Oct 2026:

```sql
select count(*) as messages, count(distinct thread_id) as threads, count(distinct organization_id) as workspaces
from crm_message where escalation_reason like 'No calendar availability%'
```

## Proposed fix

Separate "the availability computation returned nothing" from "the calendar is unavailable". An empty result on a successful fetch should not escalate; it should take the documented fallback and ask the prospect for their times, leaving the existing failure codes as the only setup-failure escalations. Review at the same time whether availability should be defined as availability hours minus every buffered booking, since the current definition empties short windows quickly and the banner copy then misdirects the operator.

## What's included

In scope: the escalation condition in `offer-alternatives.ts` and the product decision about how buffered existing bookings reduce future availability.
Not included: the single-slot booking-time re-check (ENG-13720) and the conferencing / meeting-location fail-closed gate (ENG-13957), which are different gates.
Containment for the current population: the settings workaround below, applied per workspace.

## Regression seam

Boundary: `offer-alternatives` step output and `ctx.state.escalate`. Trigger: a booking-route turn where `getTimeSlots` succeeds with zero rows. Red before: step output carries `escalate: true` with `ESCALATION_REASONS.NO_CALENDAR_AVAILABILITY` and the workflow returns before send. Green after: no escalation, the turn routes to `ASK_FOR_PREFERENCES` and a reply is produced. Existing assertion to update: `steps/__tests__/slot-alternatives.test.ts` asserts the current escalation.

## Done when

* A successful availability fetch returning zero rows no longer sets `escalate` and no longer produces the no-calendar-availability banner.
* The affected turn produces an outbound reply asking the prospect for their preferred times.
* Genuine setup failures (`CALENDAR_DISCONNECTED`, `CALENDAR_SYNC_FAILED`, meeting-location) still escalate with their own reasons.
* A regression test proves the empty-successful-fetch path at the `offer-alternatives` / `ctx.state.escalate` seam.
* The help-centre statement about the fully-booked fallback matches shipped behaviour.

## Reports

* ENG-14008

relatedSnapshot.title: When payment gives up, stop the plan, mailboxes and domains cleanly
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

ENG-8112 documented the original seven-day warning and auto-cancel decision. The operating model was revised on 11 September 2026 after measuring how billing actually works. Inboxes are charged monthly on each subscription's own anniversary and domains yearly, so there is no advance invoice 28 or 14 days before renewal. When a payment fails we warn the customer, let the provider's retries run, then switch provider renewal off so the inboxes expire at the end of the month we have already paid for, leaving a free reactivation window. This ticket owns production enforcement across payment events, base-plan/workspace termination, Zapmail, Company One, local state, recovery and audit evidence.

**Scope narrowed 29 Sep 2026.** This ticket now owns Flow B (the plan ends because the customer did not pay), Flow C (a mailbox payment fails while the plan is fine), the reactivation window and the provider-neutral design. Three parts moved out:

* the cancel steps themselves (renewal off at the supplier, per-domain resumable billing cancel) now live in ENG-14252;
* workspace and account deletion now lives in ENG-10782;
* the Autumn event classifier, the failure reason and the day 0, 3 and 7 warnings now live in ENG-13746.

Added: on Autumn, an expired plan never pauses campaigns today, because Autumn workspaces are always treated as protected. Autumn plans that expire must run the same pause and cleanup as Whop, and the automation switch (`SUBSCRIPTION_ACCESS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`) is turned on after a dry-run review. Whether Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 is finished here or closed is an open question; recommended: close it and reuse the parts this ticket needs.

**Decided 29 Sep 2026:** no immediate cut-off. When billing stops (day 14, Stripe's final retry), supplier renewal is switched off and the mailboxes keep working until the month we have already paid the supplier for ends, then they are removed. We never cancel at the supplier early. The full timeline is on ENG-13358.

## Problem in plain English

When a mailbox payment fails, a base workspace plan is cancelled, or a workspace is deleted, customer access and Zapmail supplier billing can drift apart. Acquisity may stop collecting mailbox revenue while the Zapmail domain subscription remains live and billable.

A deletion can also remove the local records needed to find the supplier subscription later. One failed step can leave the mailbox active in Zapmail, connected in Company One, hidden locally, or some combination of those states.

## Confirmed production gap

The production Autumn webhook transport is configured and receiving signed events, but the current handler only acts on new, renew, upgrade and downgrade base-plan transitions. It accepts `past_due`, `expired` and `cancel` events with HTTP 200, marks them processed and performs no mailbox cancellation or reconciliation. Since 11 August, 947 `past_due` events for domain or inbox products across 113 billing accounts reached this path without triggering supplier cleanup.

This ticket must change that behavior. Relevant events must be classified and durably enqueued. They must not be acknowledged as successfully processed when the required state transition was skipped.

## Detailed behavior

### How renewal timing actually works (measured 11 September 2026)

* Each inbox subscription renews monthly on its own anniversary. The provider charges us about a day before it, and the customer's Autumn anniversary is effectively the same moment (median gap under an hour across a 1,800 domain sample).
* So a failed customer payment has always already cost us one provider month. Accept that month rather than moving billing anchors.
* About 12% of pre-warmed domains were registered as provider stock before a customer bought them, so their provider dates differ from the customer's. Every cutoff must use the provider period end, never the customer billing date.
* Domains are yearly and renew separately. Domain renewal is owned by ENG-13745.

### What cancel means (the same steps for every reason)

1. **Stop charging.** For a customer's own cancellation, stop at the end of the period they have paid for. For non-payment, stop immediately with no further retries.
2. **Switch provider renewal off for the inbox subscription.** The inboxes keep working until the end of the month already paid for, then expire. Never cancel immediately while a paid month is running.
3. **Reactivation window.** Until that provider month ends, a customer who pays or resubscribes gets everything back: renewal back on, billing re-attached, inboxes still warm.
4. **At the end of the provider month,** once the provider confirms the inboxes expired: remove them from sending (where sending is a separate provider), mark the domain and inboxes cancelled, email the customer, and switch domain renewal off so the domain is not renewed.
5. **Campaigns pause when the plan ends,** not when the inboxes expire. This is ENG-10751 behaviour extended to Autumn.

### Flow B: the plan ends because the customer did not pay

Day 0 is the failed payment.

* Days 0 to about 14: the warnings in ENG-13746 while Autumn retries the card.
* About day 14: the plan expires. Plan, inboxes and domains all cancel using the steps above and campaigns pause. Email: "Your plan has ended. Your inboxes will be removed on {provider month end} unless you reactivate."
* 3 days before removal: "Last chance to keep your inboxes."
* At removal: "Your inboxes and domains were removed."
* Payment recovered at any point before removal: everything is restored and the customer gets "Payment received, you're all set."

### Flow C: an inbox payment fails while the plan is fine

* The same as Flow B but scoped to that domain's inboxes.
* Day 0: alert and email, "Payment failed for 12 inboxes on <domain>", with the failure reason and how to fix it. Reminders on day 3 and day 7, and a final warning 2 days before the stop date, each repeating the reason (decided 29 Sep 2026).
* At Autumn expiry: stop billing and switch provider renewal off. Take those inboxes out of active campaigns so campaigns keep sending from the rest.
* Reactivation window until the provider month ends, then removal and an email.

### Works with any inbox provider

We plan to move inboxes to Company One. The timeline, reactivation window, emails and campaign pause live on our side, keyed to a generic provider period end. Each provider adapter supplies: read an inbox subscription's period end and renewal state; switch renewal on or off; renew or restore; confirm the inboxes ended; remove them from sending; list all inventory for the daily check. Where the provider and the sending platform are the same company, the remove-from-sending step is a no-op. Confirm how Company One bills us before writing that adapter.

### Also fix

A customer cancelling a single domain goes through the same steps, ending at the end of the paid period on both sides. Today the provider is cancelled immediately while Autumn bills to period end, so the customer loses service they have paid for.

### Durable renewal and cancellation workflow

Use an explicit resumable paid lifecycle:

`notice_scheduled → customer_charge_due → paid_for_next_period → supplier_renewal_due → supplier_renewal_verified → occurrence_completed → next_occurrence_scheduled`

After failed collection:

`cure_window → supplier_nonrenewal_requested → supplier_nonrenewal_verified → supplier_period_ended → full_domain_deletion_requested → full_domain_deleted → downstream_cleanup_pending → billing_reconciled → completed`

Each transition records attempts, timestamp, idempotency key, provider response summary and last error. A retry resumes at the first incomplete transition and cannot repeat completed external actions.

For a managed inbox domain, an inbox subscription still unpaid at the safe cutoff schedules supplier non-renewal while preserving the already-paid mailbox period. Only after that period ends and conclusive provider readback confirms service ended may Acquisity delete the full associated domain and every included inbox. Customer notices must explicitly explain this whole-domain consequence.

Terminal Zapmail deletion uses Cold Mail Reseller `DELETE /domains`, which deprovisions the domain, DNS, mailboxes and associated subscriptions. Provider contract correction, verified 9 September 2026: the CMR subscription event contract says the cancel endpoint takes effect immediately and deactivates mailbox accounts. It must not be treated as end-of-cycle nonrenewal or dispatched early while promising the funded period remains available. Disabling subscription auto-renew is a separate, documented operation (`POST /subscriptions/toggle-autorenewal`). Per the provider's documented lifecycle, renewal off means the subscription goes past due at period end, gets a 7 day grace period, then expires and the mailboxes are deactivated. Verify this once in the provider sandbox, including that the paid month keeps running and that switching renewal back on restores the mailboxes, before wiring the production flow. An accepted cancellation request is not proof of full-domain cleanup.

Before completing cancellation, calculate any remaining customer-funded annual-domain value and record the explicitly approved refund, credit or no-refund outcome on the renewal occurrence. Existing historical waste handled by ENG-13362 may still require immediate full-domain deletion after fresh evidence and explicit approval.

Supplier deletion is confirmed only by the required response and conclusive domain/subscription readback. Company One and local cleanup run only after the current supplier period ended and readback confirms service ended or the domain was deleted. A future non-renewal alone is not cleanup authorization. Downstream failures remain independently retryable and cannot restart supplier service, block cost prevention or repeat a destructive action.

### Workspace and account deletion

* Workspace, billing-account, order and mailbox deletion must not cascade away supplier identity or cancellation evidence.
* Trigger the same deprovisioning workflow before destructive deletion, or retain a tombstone until cleanup is complete.
* If safety requires blocking deletion until supplier cleanup succeeds, return a clear operator/customer error.
* Cover self-service, admin, bulk, script and framework deletion entry points that can affect the scoped inventory.

### Recovery, reversals and billing access

* Payment recovery before supplier non-renewal returns the occurrence to `paid_for_next_period`.
* Recovery after non-renewal was requested requires authoritative provider reconciliation. If cancellation cannot be reversed, either provision a new explicitly approved resource or refund/credit the customer; never claim the old resource was restored.
* Recovery after provider deletion requires new checkout or approved comp and never silently recreates infrastructure.
* A refund, dispute, chargeback or credit reversal before the supplier cutoff makes the future period uncovered and enters the cure/non-renewal path.
* If money is reversed after Acquisity paid the supplier, preserve live service for the funded supplier period, flag the contradiction, prevent the next renewal and apply the approved debt/refund/access policy.
* If the customer cancels after advance collection, refund only when supplier renewal can still be safely prevented. Otherwise preserve service for the funded period and schedule the following renewal off.
* If the customer paid but supplier renewal fails, enter supplier recovery and preserve entitlement plus Company One/local linkage. Complete only after readback proves restored service, or apply the defined refund/credit outcome if it cannot be restored.
* Ending the base workspace plan does not itself prove a separately paid or approved-free inbox subscription is unpaid. Evaluate each managed inbox domain against its own inbox entitlement and supplier period.
* Customers without an active base plan retain a billing-only route to view affected resources, warning, amount, payment recovery and cancellation deadline.

## Suggested implementation route

* Extend the signed Autumn event path and scheduled renewal backstop around the same durable renewal occurrence. Name 1 advance payment failure and recovery quickly; scheduled jobs own the reminder steps, the cutoff at the provider period end and the final provider readback. Provider calls stay outside the webhook request.
* Keep provider calls out of the webhook request. Persist the event idempotently, enqueue the durable workflow, and return success only after the required transition has been recorded.
* Route delinquency deadlines, base-plan termination and workspace deletion through one shared cancellation orchestrator.
* Build the state machine on durable records introduced by the entitlement ticket.
* Derive idempotency from the immutable entitlement plus cancellation occurrence, not from a domain name or scheduler run.
* Reuse the existing Cold Mail Reseller cancellation audit foundation where it satisfies these guarantees.
* Add operational alerts and an admin view for incomplete or repeatedly failing transitions.

## Done when

* the existing Autumn webhook no longer acknowledges and discards relevant `past_due`, `expired` or `cancel` events;
* tests prove the exact event scenarios above enqueue one idempotent transition and irrelevant products remain ignored;
* every cutoff is derived from the provider period end, and duplicate events cannot reset a deadline or the notification history;
* duplicate events cannot reset grace or duplicate cancellation;
* payment recovery before supplier cancellation stops pending removal;
* supplier, Company One, local and billing steps are resumable and individually auditable;
* base-plan cancellation and every workspace deletion path trigger the same guarantees;
* deletion cannot erase the evidence needed to finish cleanup;
* full-domain supplier deletion is verified against the exact domain, supplier subscription and included mailbox quantity;
* `/subscriptions/cancel` cannot be mistaken for completed full-domain offboarding;
* active campaigns are recorded and paused before Company One removal, while Company One or local failure cannot block or repeat confirmed Zapmail deletion;
* incomplete workflows alert with the failed transition, age and estimated monthly supplier cost;
* integration tests cover payment recovery before and after supplier cancellation, duplicate events, partial provider failure, workspace deletion with active mailboxes and retry from every transition.
* customer notices identify the full affected domain/inboxes, amount, charge date, cutoff and whole-domain deletion consequence;
* provider non-renewal preserves the already-paid period and never authorizes early Company One/local disconnection;
* an unpaid managed inbox-domain subscription can delete the full domain only after period-end readback and deterministic annual-domain refund/credit/no-refund handling;
* deadlines are derived from authoritative supplier timestamps and stored in UTC; missing or drifting dates become operator exceptions;
* changed quantity, price or renewal timestamp invalidates the stale occurrence before collection;
* paid customer/supplier renewal failure enters recovery and ends only in verified restored service or deterministic refund/credit;
* tests cover payment recovery racing the cutoff, duplicate scheduler/webhook delivery, provider timeout after non-renewal, and two workers claiming the same occurrence;
* the base-plan cascade runs: plan expiry cancels inboxes and domains through the same steps, and campaigns pause at plan expiry;
* Flow C removes only the unpaid domain's inboxes while other campaigns keep sending;
* paying inside the reactivation window restores everything with no new setup or provisioning;
* no provider inbox stays live with renewal on for a customer who is not paying, checked by the daily read.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the shared cancel steps.
* ENG-13746, for the event classifier and warnings.

Do not run this at the same time as ENG-11454: both add a "stop at plan end" step, and whichever lands second reuses the first.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

### Existing-inbox management implementation slice (9 September 2026)

After ENG-13526, James confirmed that Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 must provide one owner/admin link to see all existing inbox groups, including active paid, free and credit-funded groups, with actual customer prices and current service periods. Clients can keep all, cancel all, or keep some whole domain groups and cancel others. Choices and their consequences must be reviewed before confirmation.

Keeping a group must recover any exact existing invoice without duplicating it, repair future payment collection where needed, and establish or restore recurring billing for retained inboxes without purchasing or provisioning new ones. Paying an invoice alone is not completion. Show invoice liabilities separately from future monthly charges. Preserve paid siblings, allocate shared coverage once, and keep annual domain/platform rights separate. Cancellation must record and verify exact billing and supplier effects, preserve funded periods, and show requested, scheduled, pending and completed states honestly. Promises, internal budgets and reversals require their recorded decisions before any automatic demand.

This scope supersedes the earlier invoice-only and selection-only implementation limitation. It retains this ticket's existing ownership and broader lifecycle contract, and reuses ENG-13359 entitlement and ENG-13361 reconciliation work. Unsupported or ambiguous provider actions must have a specific guided resolution and must not be reported as completed.

Implementation, tests and the draft PR are authorized, including a dedicated access-protected preview using a separate synthetic database and Autumn/Stripe test credentials. Production issuance, notices, real charges/refunds, production subscription changes, supplier cancellations, rollout and merge are not authorized. Outreach sending remains dependent on a verified working flow. This slice does not mark the lifecycle programme or estate cleanup complete.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reps pick a meeting outcome on the meeting card
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep records what a meeting meant by picking from the same workspace outcome list, limited to outcomes that apply to meetings.

## Problem

Meetings have attendance (show or no-show) but no way to record the business result. Close shares one outcome list between calls and meetings and reports on it.

## Proposed fix

Put the outcome picker on the meeting card, save the choice on the meeting and its timeline event, and keep attendance as it is.

## What's included

* The picker on the existing meeting card.
* Saving on the meeting and its timeline event together.
* Archived handling as on calls.

Excluded: attendance, which stays a separate field and is shown per Show meeting outcomes in CRM Activity; the redesigned meeting card and its outcome pill, which Koppany builds in ENG-13803.

## Blocked by

* Every workspace gets its own outcome list, seeded from today's call results
* Reps pick a call outcome in the call dock and on the call card

## How it should work

The picker offers selectable outcomes that apply to meetings. Saving writes the meeting and its event together. A meeting with no outcome shows none. Archived outcomes show greyed on meetings that have them and are not offered. Attendance and outcome are independent: marking a no-show does not change the outcome and vice versa. A failed save keeps the previous value and shows an error.

## Who can do what

Anyone who can open the meeting and change its attendance today can set its outcome.

## What the user sees

An outcome label on the meeting card, editable in place, beside the existing attendance state. The empty picker states that no outcomes apply to meetings. Follows the current app styling; the redesign restyles it later.

## Done when

- [ ] Picking an outcome on a meeting saves it and it survives reload.
- [ ] The picker shows only meeting-applicable outcomes.
- [ ] Changing attendance leaves the outcome unchanged.
- [ ] An archived outcome shows on an old meeting and is absent from the picker.
- [ ] The meeting timeline event carries the outcome reference.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Calls and meetings share one outcome vocabulary, and Koppany's redesigned card can read the meeting outcome without further data work.

## Implementation context

* Reuse the picker from ENG-13848.
* Attendance keeps its existing storage and history.
* Coordinate with Koppany so the appointment migration from ENG-13846 and his origin change land in a known order.

relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A meeting can hold many recordings (gallery view, speaker view, audio only, transcript), guests show whether they accepted, meetings carry an outcome, and Zoom cloud recordings attach to the right meeting automatically and play from Zoom, as in Close.

## Why

Close shows several Zoom assets per meeting; Acquisity's Recall notetaker tables are vendor-specific and cannot point at an appointment, and legacy `crm_meeting` has 6 rows. A sibling asset table keeps 500k Recall recordings untouched. What follows Close: linked Zoom cloud recordings for calendar-linked meetings (Close does not store them). What goes beyond Close: switching our own Zoom meetings to cloud auto-recording behind a toggle.

## Close reference

<url> <url> <url>

## Execution order

Meeting assets first, then Zoom sync. Zoom sync shares scope and re-consent work with ENG-13164 and matching with ENG-13163, so it waits for ENG-13164.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR incorrectly claims time slots are taken, attempts to rebook, repeat
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Found Problem

**\*\* This bug happened on Nov-13, 2025. So, any previous tickets adjacent to this issue deployed before then did not solve the issue.** \*\*

The AI SDR is incorrectly reporting that time slots are taken/booked when the user's calendar actually shows those times as available. This creates a frustrating loop where:

1. SDR confirms a booking
2. SDR immediately says that time is now taken
3. SDR offers alternative times
4. Prospect accepts the alternative
5. SDR again says that time is taken

## Found Problem

The AI SDR is continuing to attempt scheduling additional meetings even after a lead has confirmed receipt of a meeting invitation and the meeting has been successfully scheduled. This results in:

1. **Redundant scheduling attempts**: AI SDR keeps trying to schedule meetings that are already scheduled
2. **Confusing lead experience**: Leads receive multiple scheduling messages after they've already confirmed
3. **No confirmation detection**: System doesn't recognize when a meeting invite has been sent and confirmed

1. AI SDR sends meeting invitation to lead (Name 19 - Interview Series Invitation)
2. Lead confirms they received the meeting invite ("I got it")
3. Meeting invitation is successfully sent and scheduled

relatedSnapshot.title: Meetings link to the deal owned by the meeting host, not the SDR deal
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a closer's meeting belongs to a person who has several deals, the meeting should link to the deal the closer owns. Today My Day often shows the person's SDR deal on the closer's meeting, or no deal at all, and the same wrong answer feeds booking attribution on Floor Command.

## Problem

A closer opens My Day and sees a meeting booked with them. The deal on the card is the person's webinar SDR deal, not the Closer deal they own. Opening the deal from the card takes them to the wrong pipeline, and outcomes, missed-work prompts and the action queue act on that wrong deal.

The meeting's deal is chosen by trying a fixed list of sources and taking the first that gives exactly one deal: the booking's own deal, the conversation's deal, deals that have a meeting event for this appointment, then all of the person's deals. It never checks who owns a deal or which pipeline it is in. That fails two ways in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace (24 Sep, production read-only):

* **SDR deal chosen.** Booking workflows create the meeting a second before the Closer deal. The meeting event is written onto the only deal that exists at that moment, the SDR deal, and from then on that one tagged deal always wins. 216 closer meetings in the last 30 days are stuck this way. For 214 of them, the host owns the Closer deal. About 181 Payment Support meetings are stuck the same way.
* **No deal chosen.** Calendly bookings write no meeting event, so the person's deals are checked next. The person has both an SDR and a Closer deal, and two matches means no deal. 23 closer meetings in the next week are in this state.

Since ENG-14180 shipped (24 Sep 10:00 UTC), new bookings are also stamped with a deal using the same rules, so a wrong answer is now stored on the booking too. 4 bookings so far were stamped with the SDR deal while the host owns another deal.

## User experience

Nothing new to learn. The closer's meeting card on My Day, the action queue, outcome prompts and missed work all show the deal the closer owns. Floor Command credits the booking to that deal and its pipeline.

## What's included

* After the explicit sources (the booking's own deal, then conversation deals), look at the tagged deals and the person's deals together. If exactly one of them is owned by the meeting host, use it. Otherwise keep today's order unchanged.
* Apply this everywhere the rule is used: My Day calls, action queue, outcome prompts, missed work and booking deal stamping. The stamper currently passes no host and must pass it.
* A dry-run-first way to re-stamp bookings already stamped with a deal the host does not own when a host-owned deal exists, writing the same audit entry the stamper writes.
* Not included: removing the SDR meeting events. They are a correct record of activity on the person.

## Done when

* A closer meeting for a person with an SDR deal and a host-owned Closer deal shows the Closer deal on My Day, whether the SDR deal has a meeting event or not.
* A meeting with no host-owned deal behaves exactly as today.
* New bookings are stamped with the host-owned deal.
* The re-stamp dry run lists the affected bookings per workspace, and the apply run fixes them with audit entries.
* Tests cover: SDR event only, both deals with no events, no host-owned deal, two host-owned deals, booking deal present.

## Implementation context

* Name 20 with evidence, file references and the post-merge re-stamp plan: AI context.md
* James decided on 24 Sep to apply the host-owned rule everywhere, including Floor Command attribution, not only My Day.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR rebooks lost meetings and reconfirms meetings booked days ahead
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a booked meeting falls through, the AI offers to rebook the same day, with fresh times. Meetings booked 3 or more days out get a short reconfirmation the day before. Today 88% of lost meetings never get a message, and meetings booked far ahead are lost more often.

## Problem

* About 160 AI SDR meetings a week are lost after booking: the prospect declines the invite, the event is removed, or it is cancelled in a synced calendar.
* 88% of those threads get no message within 14 days, and only 1.9% rebook. The thread usually still says "booked", which blocks follow-ups.
* Meetings booked 5 or more days ahead are lost at about 20%, against about 12% for meetings under 3 days away. Nothing reconfirms them.

## User experience

* **Prospect declines or cancels:** within an hour, in the same thread and from the same sender, they get a short note: "no problem, here are a few other times", with live times, or "tell me a day that suits".
  * One reminder 4 days later if they don't reply, then stop.
  * The thread's status changes from "booked" back to "times offered".
* **The host removed the event** (it may be on our side): the deal owner and workspace owner get an alert first, and no email goes to the prospect until someone confirms it should.
* **Meeting booked 3 or more days out:** about 24 hours before, the prospect gets a two-line confirmation:
  * the meeting time in their time zone;
  * "reply here if you need to move it".

  Nothing is sent for meetings booked less than 3 days out, or ones already cancelled.

## What's included

1. **Lost-meeting trigger.** When an AI SDR appointment becomes cancelled or rejected:
   * Prospect-side (rejected invite, cancelled by the prospect) and not a reschedule: reset the thread from "booked", then send the rebook email using the winning writer arm with situation `MEETING_LOST`, with live times (as in ENG-14760). Schedule one follow-up 4 days later.
   * Host-side ("event removed from the host's calendar"): alert the owners, and create a CRM task to decide.
2. **Reconfirmation job.** On AI SDR appointment creation, if the meeting is 3 or more days away, sleep until 24 hours before. Check it's still scheduled, then send the confirmation, written by code from a fixed template with the time filled in by code. No model.
3. Both go through the same validator: do-not-contact, AI SDR enabled, workspace active, human takeover.
4. Each has its own switch per workspace (default on), and both are counted in the weekly report: rebook rate, and show-up rate where attendance is known.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14758: the new writer and its checks, used for the rebook email.
* ENG-14760: live times, used in the rebook email.

## Done when

- [ ] In preview, declining an AI SDR invite produces a rebook email with live times within an hour, and the thread is no longer "booked".
- [ ] A host-side removal creates an owner alert and task, and sends no prospect email.
- [ ] A reschedule (old appointment superseded by a new one) triggers nothing.
- [ ] A meeting booked 4 days out gets exactly one confirmation about 24 hours before, with the correct local time. A meeting booked 1 day out gets none. A meeting cancelled before the reminder time gets none.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests cover each path above.

## Implementation context

* Plan and evidence: AI SDR Follow-ups v2
* Supersedes ENG-8381 (configurable meeting reminders) for AI SDR meetings.
* Triggers, status values and tests are in this ticket's AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM v2: Meetings
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a workspace has the CRM v2 flag on, Meetings, Recordings and a single recording show the redesign, built to the production cut. Reps keep everything they can do today on these pages. With the flag off, nothing changes.

## User experience

* **Calendar (Meetings):** a rail with a mini month, my and team calendars (the on and off choice is remembered, as today), a Connect calendar link to calendar settings, and a call type filter. Day / Week / Month with keyboard keys, a now-line, Hide weekends, Calendar / List, search, Join and Add appointment. Events are coloured by calendar. Meetings that clash sit side by side. Times show in the rep's saved time zone, as today. Export and Edit meeting types stay in a small More menu.
* **Appointment sheet:** view, edit and create with today's fields (title, call type, date and time, host, meeting link, location, attendees, notes). Reschedule, Cancel (no "tell the contact"), Delete for people allowed to delete, and Join. Attendance (took place, host no-show, prospect no-show, awaiting host) and the meeting outcome (ENG-13850) are two separate controls. The person links to their record only when their email matches one contact exactly.
* **Recordings** (workspaces with live connect, not client members): four stats, Host / Participant / Company / Comments filters, Mine / Everyone, ranges, sorts, cards, Match for an unmatched or unclear attendee, the upcoming list, and add the bot by link (owners and admins).
* **Recording page:** player with speed, summary, action items, transcript, chapters, speakers, comments, linked records, talk time, Ask, Share, and Download (video and transcript). A recording that is still processing shows today's "Recording processing" placeholder.
* **Phones:** with the flag on, these pages say "Open this on a computer", as the design language sets for Meetings.

## Decisions taken (James can veto)

* Events coloured by calendar; call-type colours are a follow-up.
* Outcome and attendance are two controls. No default meeting outcomes are seeded; an empty list says so and points to settings.
* The Call log tab is left out (ENG-14217).
* Meeting assets, guest responses and "no longer available" (ENG-13803, Acquisity/Acquisity#6408, Acquisity/Acquisity#6464): the published production cut keeps none of them on these pages, and today they show only in the record timeline, so this build adds none. They are on ENG-14216.
* Open contact goes to the full record page, as the cut draws it; switching to the record drawer is a follow-up.

## Not included (tracked elsewhere)

* Everything else the production cut hides is on ENG-14216.
* Recordings are not linked to appointments and have no outcome until ENG-13540.

## Done when

* With the flag on, the three pages match the production cut, with the differences listed in the PR, and pass browser QA in light and dark, 1440 / 1650 / 1920, phone width, reduced motion and keyboard only.
* With the flag off, the pages and their page-open events are unchanged.
* `tool.opened` with the v2 variant is seen landing in PostHog for Meetings, Recordings and a recording, or reported as unverified with the reason.

## Implementation context

Existing procedures only, plus one field: the appointment detail read also returns the saved outcome (same row, same access checks). Standard risk; rollback is turning the flag off. Builds on ENG-14184 and ENG-14190. Design links are attached; they're private until James shares them.
